doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Army, politics and jazz in Cuba
title: Drafted into the army and discharged early
summary: He left high school at 15-16 for the army, served about two and a half years, and was released early thanks to a commander who liked to compose.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: At what age did you leave high school?
When I was 15, 16, because then they called me for the army.
So around 15 or 16 you went into the army?
I went into the army, yea.
How long were you in the army?
Almost three years, two years and a half. It was supposed to be three years, but I get rid of it because of the integration of the commander who liked to compose music. The
Commandante Almay, that was his name. He loved to compose the little songs like that, and I recorded some of his pieces, and then he liberated me from the army in six month.
So, you were in the army until you were about 18 years old?
